findings.reason: The protected app-local solution is compact, conventional, and interview-ready. values makes the non-mutating sorted copy explicit; left and right are standard two-pointer endpoints; pair_sum and best state their roles directly; and the strict comparison and no-solution sentinel remain visible in the main loop. No material correctness, robustness, complexity, clarity, or maintainability defect justifies a candidate.

Sorting preserves every value and multiplicity while making pair sums monotone. When values[left] + values[right] is below k, right is the largest remaining partner for that left endpoint, so no smaller partner can improve the recorded valid sum and advancing left is safe. When the sum is at least k, the current right value cannot form a valid pair with any remaining value at or to the right of left, so decrementing right is safe. left < right enforces distinct indices, best retains the maximum, and its initial -1 remains exactly when no valid pair exists.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1099, Python as the user-facing language, and native Solution.twoSumLessThanK. Authenticated source evidence confirms i < j, nums[i] + nums[j] as the candidate sum, strict sum < k eligibility, maximum selection, -1 when absent, 1 <= nums.length <= 100, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 2000. The solve(nums, k) adapter preserves all of those semantics.

The protected app-local solve.py and immutable leetcode.py bound to verified submission 2067627255 have identical executable bodies: both create the same sorted copy, initialize the same endpoints and sentinel, compute the same pair sum, take the same pointer transitions, update the same maximum, and return the same value. Differences are limited to the app solve function versus LeetCode Solution.twoSumLessThanK method and the native List annotation/import.

The three hidden workloads grow arrays through 16, 40, and 100 elements with every pair below k, forcing exhaustive enumeration to inspect the complete quadratic pair set while the protected target sorts and scans once. The exact protected source passed all eight visible cases and all three tiers with relative growth exponent -0.00 and a 1.03x largest runtime ratio. An independently correct all-pairs control preserved every output but failed only scaling at +1.24 and 21.88x, distinguishing O(n log n) sorting plus scanning from O(n^2) enumeration.

The Approach accurately derives sorted monotonicity, the safe left advance after a valid sum, the safe right decrease after an invalid sum, and maximum tracking with a -1 sentinel. Its O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary-space bounds match the sorted-copy implementation and branch manifest, and its alternatives and edge cases cover all-pairs enumeration, binary search, strict threshold equality, duplicate values at distinct positions, fewer than two elements, and universally invalid sums.

The modular Reference preserves the integer-array and threshold inputs, distinct indices ordered as i < j, strict inequality, maximum eligible sum, -1 fallback, all three exact constraints, and both source examples with their explanations. It adds no tables, diagrams, hints, notes, or follow-up absent from the source.

A fresh authenticated review of the live Premium statement verified exactly two explained examples, three constraints, and no hints, notes, follow-up, tables, images, or diagrams. source_fidelity.json binds the independently written modular Reference to live content hash 3e79cf838c7fd454443933eab8a14094e83230041b4fbb15d7e4fef98204ea52 and validates with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact nums and k inputs, outputs 58 and -1, and explanations appear first and in source order as sample-1 and sample-2.

All eight ordinary correctness fixtures are visible samples or trials. They cover a nontrivial interior optimum, no valid pair, one-element input, equal values at distinct indices, strict exclusion of a sum equal to k, unsorted values, minimum nums and k values, and simultaneous maximum length, value, and k boundaries.

Every case respects 1 <= nums.length <= 100, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 2000. The maximum-bound fixture contains exactly 100 values and requires the strict optimum 999 + 1000 = 1999 below k = 2000.

An independent oracle enumerates unordered index pairs with itertools.combinations, filters their sums by the strict threshold, and takes the maximum with -1 as the empty default. It shares neither sorting nor pointer transitions with the reviewed solution.

The oracle, protected app-local function, immutable native Solution method, and independently written nested-loop control agreed on all eleven authored correctness-plus-benchmark outputs, 5000 deterministic random legal inputs of lengths one through 100, and seven explicit boundaries. Random data covered the full value and k ranges, duplicates, valid and invalid sums, singleton arrays, and both dense and sparse eligible-pair sets.

The 16-, 40-, and 100-element workloads remain hidden and performance-only, use size consistently as n, force the complete all-pairs path, and span 6.25x. The quadratic control failed only scaling at +1.24 and 21.88x, while the protected solution passed at -0.00 and 1.03x; benchmark calibration is fit and benchmark.json was not edited.
